title: MTU fragmentation causing control plane reachability flaps — retrospective
content:
Summary:

- Impact: Intermittent control plane RPC failures and increased RPC latencies for ~45 minutes across a single private deployment customer (cust-77). No data plane inference requests were dropped, but control plane healthchecks and agent heartbeats failed intermittently causing rollout delays and temporary inability to scale worker pools.
- Scope: One on-prem cluster connected via customer-managed firewall + VXLAN overlay. Affected control-plane nodes (3/5) experienced transient connectivity loss to the control plane leader.
- Severity: Sev2 (customer-managed infra causing Redwood control-plane degradation)

Initial observations and notable logs: (collected during oncall)
- Control plane logs showed repeated RPC timeout errors: "context deadline exceeded" and "connection reset by peer" with bursts at 16:12–16:20 UTC.
- Network team tcpdump from edge showed lots of ICMP "fragmentation needed" (Type 3, Code 4) messages from customer firewall IP to our VTEP IP.
- Kernel counters on control-plane hosts showed increasing "IP6Frag"/"IPFragTrags" style counters and VXLAN statistics with dropped fragments.
- Customer firewall rules had an explicit MSS/MTU clamp to 1400 on outbound SYNs for their public subnet. They also were applying DF bit policies for some tunnels.

Timeline (UTC):
- 16:07: first SLO alert (controlplane RPC p99 > 1s)
- 16:10: SRE oncall paged; initial triage flagged RPC timeouts between control-plane leader and follower nodes.
- 16:12: packet captures from VTEP and host revealed fragmented UDP encapsulated VXLAN packets larger than path MTU; ICMP "fragmentation needed" traced back to customer firewall.
- 16:17: mitigation attempt #1: temporarily reduced control-plane MTU on affected hosts from 1500 to 1400 using ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 1400. Partial recovery of RPC stability (p99 down but bursts persisted).
- 16:28: customer applied a firewall config change (removed redundant MTU clamp) after collaboration with customer network ops.
- 16:33: system stabilized; final post-fix monitoring OK by 16:48.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
1) Customer firewall was performing MTU/MSS clamping to 1400 for TCP flows and was dropping or returning ICMP fragmentation-needed for UDP/VXLAN encapsulated control-plane packets, depending on DF bit behavior.
2) VXLAN overlay adds ~50 bytes of overhead (outer UDP+VXLAN+GTP/metadata in some configs) resulting in inner control-plane packets that exceeded the path MTU when hosts kept inner MTU at 1500.
3) Because some devices on the path block or rate-limit ICMP type 3 messages (or rewrite DF behavior) path MTU discovery failed, leading to fragmentation/drops and intermittent RPC failures.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- ICMP fragmentation-needed messages observed with MTU=1400 in payload path MTU field.
- tcpdump shows original packets sized ~1460–1480 with VXLAN overhead > 1500 on the wire.
- After forcing host MTU to 1400, fragmentation/ICMP events dropped significantly and RPC timeouts ceased.
- Customer firewall logs correlate with blocked fragmented UDP/large UDP packets.

Why customer traffic/DF combined to break control plane but not data plane:
- Control plane uses gRPC over TCP for some operations but also uses large UDP-encapsulated heartbeats in our private packaging. Fragmentation handling for TCP vs UDP across their firewall differed; the firewall's MSS clamp handled TCP flows more gracefully, but UDP path fragmentation was being blocked. Data plane inference flows were using smaller payloads or different ports/have been optimized for fragmentation/MTU via previous traffic shaping and so were unaffected.

Reproduction notes (dev environment):
- Repro done in lab by creating a VXLAN overlay with MTU 1500 on hosts and simulating an inline firewall that rejects fragmented UDP. Observed identical failure modes for control RPCs if DF set and MTU mismatch > ~30 bytes.
- Commands used:
  - tcpdump -i vxlan0 -w /tmp/cp-frag.pcap udp and tcp port 15001
  - ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 1400
  - ip -s link show vxlan0
  - sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=0 (ensure PMTU discovery enabled)
  - iptables -A FORWARD -p udp --fragile -j LOG (debug frag behavior)

Immediate mitigations applied during incident: (timeline matched above)
- Reduced host VXLAN MTU from 1500 to 1400 on affected control-plane hosts (works but is brittle as a long-term setting).
- Coordinated with customer to remove the aggressive MTU clamp and ensure ICMP fragmentation-needed was not blocked.

Longer-term mitigations and proposals (ranked):
1) Default control-plane overlay MTU reduction: change default VXLAN/dev MTU to 1450 (or configurable per-deployment) so VXLAN + inner payload rarely exceeds common clamped MTU values. Owner: eng-private-deployments (Luca). ETA: 2 weeks.
2) Implement active PMTU probe metric and alert: emit a controlplane metric 'controlplane.pmtu.frag_rate' derived from kernel counters and packet drops, alert when > baseline. Owner: observability team (Rina). ETA: 1 week for basic dashboard; 3 weeks for automated alert.
3) Harden runbook: add an "MTU mismatch" section in private-deployments runbook with commands to check ICMP type3, kernel frag counters, and temporary MTU change steps. Include checklist for customer L2/L3 validations. Owner: SRE docs (Samira). ETA: 3 days.
4) Explicit handshake to surface customer-side MTU clamps in onboarding: we add a question to our deployment checklist for customers using on-prem firewalls/VPNs: "Do you apply MSS/MTU clamping or DF policies?" Owner: solutions-eng. ETA: next sprint.
5) Control-plane encapsulation tuning: evaluate reducing VXLAN overhead (trim optional metadata) or switch to a fragmentation-friendly encapsulation for control RPCs. Owner: serving-runtime networking (Daniel). ETA: design 4 weeks.
6) Add defensive host-level sysctl: enable net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on control-plane hosts to probe smaller MTU on repeated failures. Documented as fallback only. Owner: platform-engineering. ETA: 1 week.

Runbook patch (draft) — place into private-deployments runbook under "Network MTU / fragmentation"
- Triage steps:
  - Check RPC errors in control-plane logs and correlate with time window.
  - Run: ip -s link show dev vxlan0 and ip addr show; note MTU and dropped/fragments counters.
  - tcpdump capture on VTEP and host: tcpdump -nn -i any 'icmp or (udp and host <peer_ip>)' -w /tmp/frag.pcap
  - If ICMP type3 code4 present, note MTU value encoded and trace source via firewall logs.
  - Temporary mitigation: ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 1400 (announce to customer and schedule rollback).
  - Escalation path: contact customer network ops, provide pcap and firewall log snippets, request removal of DF/MTU clamp or allow ICMP type3.

Testing checklist for customer onboarding (new items):
- Verify that intermediate firewalls/NATs do not silently drop ICMP type 3.
- Confirm whether any tunnel endpoints rewrite DF bit or enforce MSS clamping; request exact config snippets.
- Run a quick PMTU probe from host to VTEP and across suspected path: tracepath and ping -M do -s <size>.

Instrumentation changes required: (short list)
- Add metric: controlplane.packet.fragmented_count (incremented from host during capture/driver counters).
- Add alert runbook link in p99 RPC latency rule to MTU-frag runbook.
- Add synthetic health-check that sends a large control-plane message (size ~ 1200 bytes) across overlay and verifies no fragmentation needed reply.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do other customers with heavy firewall policies have similar but silent events? Should we proactively scan in next infra sweep? (Action: solutions-eng to run a 10-customer MTU survey)
- Is reducing default VXLAN MTU to 1450 acceptable for all on-prem customers (some performance-sensitive customers may prefer 1500)? We need a per-deployment knob.
- Can we detect customer-side MTU clamps during automated deployment (i.e., during initial healthcheck)? Research item.

Post-incident notes (behavioral):
- Good cross-team collaboration: customer network ops responded within 10 minutes of being engaged which helped expedite rollback.
- Oncall didn't initially look at ICMP type3 metrics — add to default SRE triage checklist.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Luca: PR to set default vxlan mtu to 1450 in deployment templates, include feature flag. ETA 2026-05-02.
- Rina: dashboard + alert for pmtu frag metric. ETA 2026-04-27.
- Samira: runbook section and update triage checklist. ETA 2026-04-22.
- Daniel: design doc for encapsulation change / metadata trimming. ETA 2026-05-12.
- Solutions-eng: customer MTU/clamp survey. ETA 2026-05-05.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets collected during oncall:
- ip -s link show vxlan0
- ethtool -S <native_iface> | grep frag
- sudo tcpdump -i any -nn -s 0 -w /tmp/frag.pcap 'icmp or udp'
- sudo tc qdisc show dev vxlan0
- sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
- ping -M do -s 1400 <peer> (to simulate DF behavior)

References: linked ticket SRE-2981 (incident), slack thread (internal discussion), PR #412 (temporary default MTU change).

Notes to self / rough ideas: keep the temporary host-MTU change step as documented but avoid recommending it as default without per-customer consideration. Also check whether our overlay headers vary by runtime (some older agents add extra metadata) — could be trimmed to reduce necessary MTU headroom.

End of doc.
